abstract: |
  This project examines job satisfaction among employed people in Switzerland using 21 annual waves of the Swiss Household Panel (2004–2024). The employed sample contains 124,769 respondent-year observations. We investigate occupational and demographic differences, changes around the 2009 financial crisis, the 2015 Swiss franc shock and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, and whether occupational gaps vary across broader economic periods. Exploratory analysis and preliminary OLS regressions with respondent-clustered standard errors show that satisfaction differs across groups and years. The unweighted annual mean declined from 8.212 in 2004 to 7.815 in 2024, and occupation-by-period interactions are jointly significant. The results describe associations, not causal effects, and are subject to missingness, changing sample composition and survey-design limitations.
